description: The single best free resource to start with for each language and subject, plus one for practice, one for reference and one for what to do next.

meta.how_it_relates: Every resource_id points to an entry in learning_resources.json. Every language_id matches programming_languages.json.

fields.best_free: The one resource to start with. Always free.
fields.practice: Where to practise what you learned (often Exercism). Always free.
fields.reference: What to open when you need to look something up. Always free. Can be empty.
fields.next_step: What to do after the basics. Check its cost field because a few next steps are freemium.
fields.note: Extra advice or an honest warning.

meta.honesty_note: These are judgement calls, not rankings from a test. Everything picked to start with is free. Some languages (PHP, Ruby, Kotlin, R, Dart, Assembly) have fewer great free beginner resources, and the notes say so.
meta.link_check_note: Links come from learning_resources.json and were written from memory, so click through to confirm.

best_free.name: Beej's Guide to C Programming
best_free.why: Clear, friendly, covers pointers and memory properly, which is the hard part of C.

next_step.name: CMU 15-213: Computer Systems
next_step.why: Shows what your C code does inside the computer.

languages.name: C++

best_free.name: LearnCpp.com
best_free.why: The most complete free C++ course, written for modern C++ and updated often.

next_step.name: C++ Core Guidelines
next_step.why: Teaches you to write safe, clean C++ once the basics are comfortable.

languages.note: CSES is the practice pick because C++ jobs and interviews lean on algorithm problems.

languages.name: Rust

best_free.name: The Rust Programming Language
best_free.why: The official book, and the one everyone else's material is built around.

next_step.name: Build Your Own X
next_step.why: Build a small real tool to make ownership rules stick.

languages.note: Do Rustlings alongside the book, chapter by chapter.

languages.name: Assembly

best_free.name: Nand2Tetris
best_free.why: Builds a computer from logic gates up, so assembly finally makes sense as hardware.

next_step.name: CMU 15-213: Computer Systems
next_step.why: Connects assembly to real programs and memory.

languages.note: Azeria is the pick for real-world ARM assembly. Nand2Tetris teaches its own simple chip first.

best_free.name: A Tour of Go
best_free.why: Short, official, interactive, and Go is small enough that this covers most of it.

next_step.name: Learn Go with Tests
next_step.why: Teaches testing and good habits while you keep learning Go.

languages.name: Java

best_free.name: MOOC.fi Java Programming
best_free.why: A university course with lots of exercises, and it teaches object-oriented thinking well.

next_step.name: Spring Guides
next_step.why: Spring is what most Java jobs actually use.

languages.note: Learn core Java first, then move to Spring.

languages.name: C#

best_free.name: .NET Learn
best_free.why: Microsoft's own free learning paths, kept current, with a clear route to web apps.

next_step.name: Unity Learn
next_step.why: Pick this if games are your goal; otherwise continue with ASP.NET Core on the same site.

languages.note: Unity Learn is freemium, so choose the pathways marked free.

languages.name: Python

best_free.name: Harvard CS50P (Python)
best_free.why: Free university course with exercises and a clear order, so you are never lost.

next_step.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
next_step.why: Practical projects that make you use what you learned.

languages.note: For web: Django tutorial. For data and AI: Kaggle Learn. Both are in the main resources file.

languages.name: JavaScript

best_free.name: The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
best_free.why: Goes from beginner to deep topics like async and closures, with exercises.

next_step.name: Full Stack Open
next_step.why: Builds real apps with React and Node after you know the basics.

languages.note: Learn some HTML and CSS first (MDN) if you want to use JavaScript for websites.

languages.name: TypeScript

best_free.name: TypeScript for JavaScript Programmers
best_free.why: Fastest way in if you already know JavaScript.

next_step.name: Full Stack Open
next_step.why: Uses TypeScript in a real project.

languages.note: Learn JavaScript first. Read the Handbook after this short intro.

languages.name: Kotlin

best_free.name: Kotlin Documentation - Getting Started
best_free.why: The official docs have an interactive tour, and Kotlin is simple to pick up.

next_step.name: Android Basics with Compose
next_step.why: Google's official free course for building Android apps.

languages.note: Fewer great free options than Java or Python, so the official docs are the safest base.

languages.name: Swift

best_free.name: 100 Days of SwiftUI
best_free.why: Free, step-by-step, and takes you from zero to building iPhone apps.

languages.note: You need a Mac to build apps.

languages.name: PHP

best_free.name: PHP: The Right Way
best_free.why: Teaches modern PHP habits and security, which many older tutorials skip.

next_step.name: Laravel Bootcamp
next_step.why: Laravel is what most PHP jobs use now.

languages.note: Not a first-ever-code book. If you are brand new to programming, start with a general beginner course such as CS50x first.

languages.name: Ruby

best_free.name: The Odin Project
best_free.why: Has a complete free Ruby and Rails path with projects.

next_step.name: Ruby on Rails Guides
next_step.why: The official guides for building web apps in Rails.

languages.note: Ruby has fewer great free beginner courses than other languages.

best_free.name: SQLBolt
best_free.why: Short interactive lessons you finish in an afternoon.

next_step.name: Use The Index, Luke
next_step.why: Teaches how to make queries fast.

languages.name: R

best_free.name: R for Data Science
best_free.why: The standard free book for using R on real data.

next_step.name: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
next_step.why: The statistics behind the methods, with R examples.

languages.note: R for Data Science assumes you want to work with data. For pure statistics, read ISLR alongside it.

languages.name: Dart

best_free.name: Dart Language Tour
best_free.why: Official tour of the language, short and clear.

next_step.name: Flutter Documentation
next_step.why: Most Dart jobs are Flutter app building.

languages.note: Dart is small. Most of your learning time goes into Flutter.

subjects.subject: DSA
subjects.name: Data Structures and Algorithms

best_free.name: VisuAlgo
best_free.why: Lets you watch each algorithm move step by step, which is the quickest way to understand it.

subjects.note: Read about the idea, watch it in VisuAlgo, then solve problems.

best_free.name: Nand2Tetris
best_free.why: Builds a whole computer from basic parts.

subjects.subject: DPSD
subjects.name: Digital Principles and System Design

best_free.name: All About Circuits - Digital Textbook
best_free.why: Free textbook covering gates, adders, multiplexers and flip-flops in order.

subjects.note: Neso Academy videos are a good partner if you prefer watching.

best_free.name: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
best_free.why: Free book that explains processes, memory and files in plain language.

subjects.subject: CN
subjects.name: Computer Networks

best_free.name: Cloudflare Learning Center
best_free.why: Plain explanations of DNS, HTTP and security.

subjects.note: Beej's guide is for people who also want to write network code in C.

best_free.name: Neso Academy (YouTube)
best_free.why: Syllabus-style lessons on normalisation, transactions and indexing.

subjects.subject: OOP
subjects.name: Object-Oriented Programming

best_free.name: MOOC.fi Java Programming
best_free.why: Teaches classes, objects and design through many exercises.

subjects.note: Refactoring.Guru is freemium: the website is free, the book is paid.
